picks.title: ‘Merry the Christmas Witch’ Director Estimated Movie Would Cost $80 Million — but Says With AI, He Made It for $1.5 Million (EXCLUSIVE)
picks.excerpt: Director Tom Walsh said he produced the two-hour film for $1.5 million using AI, perhaps serving as a test case for the types of projects AI can help make.
picks.rationale: Concrete budget case study ($80M estimate vs $1.5M actual) for a full-length AI-made feature; freshest and most concrete item in the pool.

picks.title: Antonio Banderas to Star in AI-Powered Feature ‘Cortes’ From Utopai Studios
picks.excerpt: The Oscar-nominated actor will star as Hernán Cortés in “Cortés,” an AI-powered feature from Utopai Studios and Ex Machina Studios now shooting in Paris.
picks.rationale: An Oscar-nominated star signs onto an AI-powered feature now shooting. That is a new production announcement, separate from Utopai's earlier tool launch.

picks.title: AI Productions Require Traditional Skills To Be Cinematic, Say Filmmakers On Kling AI Panel: “You Need Experts To Prevent Everything Looking The Same”
picks.excerpt: Filmmakers including '12.12: The Day' director Kim Sung-soo said on an ACFM & Kling AI panel in Busan that AI production still needs traditionally trained crew to keep results from looking the same.
picks.rationale: The single Busan/Kling pick: working Korean filmmakers on why AI production still needs trained crew. It is a different event from the TIFF Kling panel.

picks.title: You're Spending Too Much on Your AI Videos
picks.excerpt: Curious Refuge shares workflows for saving generation credits on an AI film so you don't waste money on bad generations.
picks.rationale: The most practical item: workflow tips for cutting generation-credit spend on AI film projects.

picks.title: Real-Time AI Worlds in Focus at Visko and Google Cloud's October 14 LA Fireside Chat
picks.excerpt: The get-together looks at AI-generated environments that respond to user input while keeping continuity, and what they could mean for previs, virtual production and games.
picks.rationale: Interactive AI-generated worlds that keep continuity, applied to previs and virtual production. Adds a tech angle and a fourth outlet.

alternates.title: Tilly Nollywood? African Filmmakers — Ready or Not — Get Set for the AI Revolution
alternates.excerpt: While generative AI has the potential to transform filmmaking in Africa, practical challenges on the continent abound.
alternates.rationale: Fresh regional feature. Held back only because Variety already has two picks (outlet cap).

alternates.title: AI Creative Summit unveils full lineup for 2026 edition
alternates.excerpt: Presented by Screen International, Broadcast and Broadcast Tech, the AI Creative Summit is expanding this year in response to unprecedented interest in AI from the creative and media industries.
alternates.rationale: Industry event lineup announcement. Credible, but lower actionability.

alternates.title: Netflix Has Used AI on About 300 Titles, but “Human Touch Is Critical,” Exec Says in Busan
alternates.excerpt: Netflix’s Asia-Pacific production head Sung Q Lee, ‘The Outlaws’ director Kang Yun-sung and Wētā FX's Kimball Thurston discussed creative possibilities, production savings and the limits of AI at the streamer’s Busan panel.
alternates.rationale: Usable only if the Deadline Kling pick is swapped out (one Busan card max), and only after confirming this panel is a different event from the Netflix Eyeline/Rustad Busan story published 2026-10-11.
